statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r is the minimum, over all subsets R of the obstacle set O = {(i,j) | 0 <= i < m, 0 <= j < n, grid[i][j] = 1}, of |R| such that (0,0) and (m-1,n-1) are connected in the graph whose vertices are all cells (i,j) with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n and (grid[i][j] = 0 or (i,j) in R), with an edge between two vertices exactly when they differ by 1 in exactly one coordinate. Equivalently, r is the minimum number of obstacle cells that must be removed so that an orthogonal path exists from the upper-left corner to the lower-right corner.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid) and n = len(grid[0]). Assume m >= 1, n >= 1, every row of grid has length n, m * n >= 2, m <= 100000, n <= 100000, m * n <= 100000, grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1 for all 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n, and grid[0][0] = grid[m-1][n-1] = 0.

statement: For every such grid, the function returns a result r; it does not fail, panic, overflow, or perform an out-of-bounds access.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid) and n = len(grid[0]). Assume m >= 1, n >= 1, every row of grid has length n, m * n >= 2, m <= 100000, n <= 100000, m * n <= 100000, grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1 for all 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n, and grid[0][0] = grid[m-1][n-1] = 0.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 0 <= r <= min(m + n - 3, |O|), where O = {(i,j) | 0 <= i < m, 0 <= j < n, grid[i][j] = 1}.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid) and n = len(grid[0]). Assume m >= 1, n >= 1, every row of grid has length n, m * n >= 2, m <= 100000, n <= 100000, m * n <= 100000, grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1 for all 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n, and grid[0][0] = grid[m-1][n-1] = 0.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there exists a finite sequence P = (p_0, ..., p_k) of cells with k >= 0, p_0 = (0,0), p_k = (m-1,n-1), each p_l = (i_l,j_l) satisfying 0 <= i_l < m and 0 <= j_l < n, and |i_{l+1}-i_l| + |j_{l+1}-j_l| = 1 for every 0 <= l < k, such that the number of distinct cells of P whose grid value is 1 is exactly r.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid) and n = len(grid[0]). Assume m >= 1, n >= 1, every row of grid has length n, m * n >= 2, m <= 100000, n <= 100000, m * n <= 100000, grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1 for all 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n, and grid[0][0] = grid[m-1][n-1] = 0.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every finite sequence P = (p_0, ..., p_k) of cells with k >= 0, p_0 = (0,0), p_k = (m-1,n-1), each p_l = (i_l,j_l) satisfying 0 <= i_l < m and 0 <= j_l < n, and |i_{l+1}-i_l| + |j_{l+1}-j_l| = 1 for every 0 <= l < k, the number of distinct cells of P whose grid value is 1 is at least r.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 0 if and only if there exists a finite sequence P = (p_0, ..., p_k) of cells with k >= 0, p_0 = (0,0), p_k = (m-1,n-1), each p_l = (i_l,j_l) satisfying 0 <= i_l < m and 0 <= j_l < n, |i_{l+1}-i_l| + |j_{l+1}-j_l| = 1 for every 0 <= l < k, and grid[i_l][j_l] = 0 for every 0 <= l <= k.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = m + n - 3.

statement: Whenever minimum_obstacles(grid) returns r and minimum_obstacles(gridT) returns rT, r = rT.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid) and n = len(grid[0]). Assume m >= 1, n >= 1, every row of grid has length n, m * n >= 2, m <= 100000, n <= 100000, m * n <= 100000, grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1 for all 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n, and grid[0][0] = grid[m-1][n-1] = 0. statement: Whenever minimum_obstacles(grid) returns r and minimum_obstacles(gridR) returns rR, r = rR.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid) and n = len(grid[0]). Assume m >= 1, n >= 1, every row of grid has length n, m * n >= 2, m <= 100000, n <= 100000, m * n <= 100000, grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1 for all 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n, and grid[0][0] = grid[m-1][n-1] = 0. statement: Whenever minimum_obstacles(g) returns r_g and minimum_obstacles(h) returns r_h, r_g <= r_h.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = min(grid[0][1], grid[1][0]).
preconditions: Let m = len(grid) and n = len(grid[0]). Assume m = 2, n = 2, grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1 for all 0 <= i < 2 and 0 <= j < 2, and grid[0][0] = grid[1][1] = 0.
